posts.title: Drawing Ăn Gì and Wishjar in C4: Small Apps With Room to Grow
posts.summary: C4 diagrams of two side projects I run in production: where state lives, how paid APIs are capped, and what would break first at ten times the traffic.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Wishjar: Vietnamese Wishes With the Right Pronouns, One Shake Away
posts.summary: Wishjar is a free web app with 1,008 Vietnamese wishes, pickup lines and captions. Pick who it's for, shake the jar and get a line with the right pronouns.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Where to Eat in Vietnam: I Built an App That Picks One Place
posts.summary: Where to eat in Vietnam? Ăn Gì is a free web app that picks one place near you or where you are heading, with directions and a food-by-province guide.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The First Five Minutes of a System Design Interview
posts.summary: Before you draw a box: the questions that change a design, a one-minute scale estimate, how to say assumptions out loud and where the gaps between boxes hide.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Keep what your code reviews learn
posts.summary: Good reviews dig up commands, edge cases and reasons, then bury them in a PR thread. How to pick what's worth keeping, where it should live, and how to keep it light.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What Thirty Days of Small Notes Can Teach You
posts.summary: One line a day for a month: what diary studies found, what to write in each note, how to read the pile on day 30, and how 326 food notes turned into an app.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Let AI Widen the Search. Keep the Judgment.
posts.summary: AI is great at listing leads fast and weak at choosing which source to trust. How to split search from judgment, with an incident example and a source receipt prompt.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Protecting Focus in a Busy Team
posts.summary: Focus breaks down at the team level, so solo hacks only go so far. What research on interruptions shows, and the norms that give engineers real thinking time back.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Designing Defaults That Fail Safely
posts.summary: Defaults decide what happens when nobody decides. How to pick ones that fail safely: closed for access, off for new flags, explicit timeouts, and fallbacks you can see.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Making Handoffs Honest About What Is Unknown
posts.summary: Why "should be fine" in a handoff hides a guess, and how to label each claim as verified, assumed or unknown so the next owner knows what to trust and what to test.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Done Means Someone Else Can Pick It Up
posts.summary: "Basically done" is a risky place to stop. What finishing properly includes, why loose ends come back to bite, and five questions to answer before you close a ticket.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Ask the AI to Name Its Assumptions First
posts.summary: AI fills the gaps in your question with guesses it rarely mentions. Why models do that, a prompt that brings them out, and how to check the ones your code rests on.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Notice Friction Before It Turns Into Blame
posts.summary: Small repeated snags turn into stories about people if nobody names them. How to spot friction early, read it as a signal about the system and fix something small.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Keep Data Contracts Small Enough to Trust
posts.summary: Wide data contracts get depended on in ways nobody planned. How to keep APIs and events small: one meaning per field, consumer-driven tests and safe schema changes.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Keep Checklists Close to the Work
posts.summary: A checklist nobody opens can't catch anything. Put short, concrete checklists at the pause points where work happens: PR templates, deploy steps, runbooks, handoffs.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Find the Way Back Before You Decide
posts.summary: Many decisions feel permanent only because nobody has described how to undo them. How to tell one-way doors from two-way doors, and how to build the way back.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Treat AI Suggestions as Draft Evidence
posts.summary: AI suggestions often sound right and turn out almost right. Treat each one as a lead: turn the claim into a check against logs, tests or source before you act on it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Making Room for the Reviewer Who Doesn't Speak First
posts.summary: Live reviews reward whoever talks first. Written context, a few minutes of reading, specific prompts and clear deadlines let careful reviewers shape the decision too.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Choose Boring Boundaries, on Purpose
posts.summary: Why good module boundaries look plain: each change lands in one place, no flag-stuffed abstractions, lines follow language and teams, and a clear rule for what crosses.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Status Updates People Can Actually Act On
posts.summary: A status update is a coordination tool. Lead with the ask, show evidence, name an owner, give a next-update time and say what readers don't need to do.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Wait for the Whole Story Before You Call It
posts.summary: The first version of what went wrong is usually too clean. Why hindsight fools us, how blameless postmortems handle it, and how to put a clock on waiting for context.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Keep AI Changes Small Enough to Actually Review
posts.summary: AI makes big diffs cheap to write, not cheap to review. How to prompt for small changes, split mixed intent and review AI-assisted PRs with real evidence.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What Good Ownership Looks Like Day to Day
posts.summary: Owning work means a clear next decision, handoffs someone else can pick up, and honest updates on what you don’t know yet. Being online all day is a different job.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Design the Escape Hatch Before Someone Builds a Back Door
posts.summary: Every production system needs emergency paths. How to build ones that are narrow, logged and rehearsed, so the 2 a.m. fix never becomes a hidden back door.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Close the Loop Before You Start the Next One
posts.summary: Before jumping to the next task, spend five minutes on the last one: what changed, how you know, what is left. It helps the next person, your planning and your own focus.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Sometimes Progress Means Taking Things Away
posts.summary: People default to adding: more tasks, more charts, more code. What research on subtraction found, why deleting counts as progress, and how to spot weight worth removing.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Let AI Write the Boring First Draft
posts.summary: AI is great at turning scattered notes into a plain first draft people can argue with. How to brief it, why plain beats polished and what the human pass must check.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Ask for Help While the Problem Is Still Small
posts.summary: Asking early feels exposed, yet people say yes more often than we expect. When to ask, how to ask in two lines, and how to answer so your team keeps asking early.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Let the Interface Tell the Truth When the System Is Struggling
posts.summary: Slow, partial, stale or uncertain: how to show real system limits on screen, what the backend must track to do it, and how to word the message so users trust it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Keep Meeting Notes Close to the Decisions They Made
posts.summary: A five-line decision block at the end of each meeting, copied into the ticket and the PR, saves the next teammate from asking why the team chose what it chose.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Relief of Finally Naming the Problem
posts.summary: "Communication issue" fixes nothing. Why a precise problem name cuts blame, points to a next step, and how to shrink a vague complaint to one sentence people can act on.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Ask Your AI Assistant What Its Answer Stands On
posts.summary: A fluent AI answer built on two files looks the same as one built on twenty. Ask which files, logs and tests it used. That beats asking it to explain itself.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Why Good Teams Surface Risk Early (Without the Panic)
posts.summary: Hidden risk only gets more expensive. How good teams name risks early, write them so they can be tested, run a premortem and react so people keep speaking up.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Designing for the Change You Can Actually See
posts.summary: Every abstraction has a running cost. How to find the changes your code has really seen, where flexibility pays off, and when a short note beats another layer.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Writing Next Steps That Actually Help
posts.summary: "We'll follow up" isn't a next step. Give it one owner, a visible verb, the evidence to bring back and a clear point to stop, and the work moves the very next morning.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Carrying Uncertainty Without Stalling the Work
posts.summary: Unknowns don't have to stop a project. Name each one specifically, decide whether it blocks, give it an owner and a next check, and decide with open questions on record.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Letting AI Draft While Humans Keep the Map
posts.summary: AI can draft a patch in seconds. Knowing where it belongs is still the team's job: what Naur and METR say about that gap, and habits for context and review.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What Small Code Reviews Teach Your Team
posts.summary: A ten-line PR rarely matters to the product, but its review teaches the team how to talk about quality. What Google's research found, and what to change in yours.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Name a Boundary, Then Give It Examples
posts.summary: A layer name on a diagram feels clear until the first real ticket arrives. Concrete examples show who owns what, what may cross and where a boundary sits wrong.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Making Handoffs Easier to Receive
posts.summary: What a handoff needs so the next person can start in minutes: status first, decisions with reasons, named risks, a clear next step, and a playback from the receiver.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What Vague Words Cost Your Team
posts.summary: Words like "cleaner" or "soon" feel harmless in a meeting and turn into rework later. Where the cost of vague language lands, and the simple habits that keep it small.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What AI Can't Know From the Prompt Alone
posts.summary: A clear prompt still leaves out the code, the logs, the domain rules and the history behind them. What a model can't see, and which evidence to hand it instead.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: How Trust Grows in Ordinary Follow-Through
posts.summary: Team trust rarely comes from big rescues. It grows from small promises kept, early heads-ups when dates slip and honest repair, with messages you can copy.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Keep Architecture Decisions Small Enough to Revisit
posts.summary: Big architecture decisions are hard to undo. How to spot the one-way doors, split the rest into small records, and write down the signal that says it's time to revisit.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: A Fuzzy Request Deserves One Shared Page
posts.summary: When a quick request grows corners, write one shared page: what changes, who it affects, real examples, open questions with owners, and the decisions made so far.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Case for a Slightly Slower First Answer
posts.summary: The first answer in a thread tends to anchor everything after it. Why a short pause with a purpose beats a fast guess, and how to buy that time without going silent.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Using AI Without Handing Over Your Judgment
posts.summary: AI can map a code path and draft a patch in seconds. What research says about confidence, security and learning, and the habits that keep the final call with you.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: How to Say "Not Yet" to a Release Without Becoming the Blocker
posts.summary: A good "not yet" names what's missing, who owns it and when you'll decide again. How to pause a release with evidence, and the options between shipping and waiting.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Interfaces That Outlive the Code Behind Them
posts.summary: How to design an interface that survives rewrites: hide what's likely to change, mind Hyrum's Law, publish late, test the promise, evolve it without breaking callers.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: When Scope Changes, Ask What Moves Out
posts.summary: New work will land mid-sprint. Make the plan visible, ask what moves out, hammer the request down and name the trade-off out loud so nobody absorbs it in silence.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Why Consistency Compounds
posts.summary: One test, one note, one clearer name a day looks like nothing. A few months later it adds up. What habit research says about consistency, and how to keep it going.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Using AI to Read a Codebase You Didn't Write
posts.summary: How to use AI in your first days on an unfamiliar codebase: prompts that trace real flows, how to check what the tool tells you and which paths to read yourself.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Your Reviewer Is the Code's First Future Reader
posts.summary: Your reviewer is the first person to read the change without your memory of it. Use that moment to move hidden context into names, tests and the PR before it fades.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Refactoring Toward a Clearer Core, One Small Step at a Time
posts.summary: Trace one business rule, pin its behavior with characterization tests, give it one home and one name, and ship small refactors that make the next change easy.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Managing Dependencies Without Finding Someone to Blame
posts.summary: Late dependencies turn into blame. Write each one down, make "owner" mean the next action, plan handoffs with slack and design the fallback before you need it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Difference Between Confidence and Evidence
posts.summary: Feeling sure is only reliable under certain conditions. When to trust a gut call, what to ask before you commit, how much evidence is enough and how to bound a claim.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: From a Great AI Demo to Behavior Users Can Depend On
posts.summary: What changes between an AI demo and production: a written behavior spec, real evals, recovery paths, guardrails for a model that gets fooled, monitoring, pinned models.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: When Silence in a Team Becomes a Signal
posts.summary: Three seconds of silence after "any concerns?" isn’t always a yes. What team silence can mean, why speaking up feels risky, and simple ways to hear it early.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Architecture Decision Records for Your Future Teammates
posts.summary: Code shows a system's shape but never the reason. A one-page decision record keeps the context, the options you rejected and the signal that says to revisit it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: A Decision Log Busy Teams Will Actually Keep
posts.summary: A decision log is a few lines per decision: what you chose, what you dropped, why, who owns it and when to revisit. A format busy teams actually keep up with.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Note You Come Back To
posts.summary: Some notes only make sense months later. Why hindsight rewrites your memory, how to write a note your future self can use, and what to do when you read it again.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Feedback Loop That Makes AI Work Better Every Week
posts.summary: The first AI draft is cheap. The value comes after: check it against evidence, record what it missed and feed that lesson back so the next request starts smarter.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: How to Ask for Help So It's Easy to Say Yes
posts.summary: People agree to help more often than we expect. How to package a clear ask, who to ask, and how to help a teammate without taking over their keyboard.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Choose the Boundary Before You Choose the Tool
posts.summary: Before you pick a queue, a database or a framework, name who owns each rule, what must stay consistent and which words mean different things. Then pick tools.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: When the Roadmap Meets Real Capacity
posts.summary: A roadmap only helps once it survives a talk about real capacity. Count the hidden work, keep priority apart from order, say no cleanly and check the plan every week.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: It Takes a Little Nerve to Write the First Rough Note
posts.summary: Why the first rough note is the hardest one to write, what Paul Graham and Anne Lamott say about bad first drafts, and a four-line template to get a messy idea down.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Cost of Trusting a Fluent AI Answer
posts.summary: Smooth AI answers feel finished before anyone checks them. Why fluency reads as truth, what the data shows it costs, and five habits that get past the polish.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: A Simple Script for Hard Feedback Conversations
posts.summary: Hard feedback goes better with a script: write down what you saw and its impact, ask for their side, agree on one visible change, then follow up when it works.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Observability Is a Design Decision
posts.summary: Whether production can explain itself depends on choices made before release: event names, one trace ID through every hop, and alerts that point at user pain.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Cross-Functional Teams Work When They Share One Outcome
posts.summary: What makes a cross-functional team real: a shared outcome, fewer handoffs, ownership with names attached, specialists who stay specialists, and disagreement put to work.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: When You're the Only Developer on the Project
posts.summary: Building software alone is fast and free, but feedback goes missing and every decision lands on you. A few habits help: decision records, borrowed review, firm basics.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What a Vector Database Actually Does, and Where It Trips Up
posts.summary: How vector databases let 'money back' find 'refund': embeddings, distance, approximate indexes like HNSW, filters, hybrid search, freshness and storage cost.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Innovation in Teams Starts With Noticing Friction
posts.summary: Most team innovation starts with someone noticing friction. How safety, slack time, user context, small experiments and clear constraints help good ideas ship.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Outbox Pattern: Stop Losing Events Between Commit and Publish
posts.summary: Why saving to the database and then publishing to a broker can lose events, how a transactional outbox closes the gap, and what relays and consumers still need.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Engineering OKRs That Measure Real Change
posts.summary: How engineering teams can write OKRs that work: key results as evidence, committed vs aspirational goals, DORA metrics without gaming, and a mid-quarter check-in.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: One New Language a Year, No Fluency Required
posts.summary: Why learning one new programming or spoken language a year pays off even if you never ship it, how to pick one that stretches you, and how to keep the year small.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: AI in Cybersecurity, on Both Sides of the Alert
posts.summary: How AI helps security teams triage alerts, review code and run incidents, how attackers use it as of November 2026, and how to keep the AI tool from becoming the hole.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Office Politics, Played in Daylight
posts.summary: Politics is what happens when facts alone can't settle a decision. How to read incentives, pre-align in the open, disagree and commit, and know when to walk away.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Do You Need a Service Mesh? Ask Your Incidents First
posts.summary: What a service mesh really does, what it can't fix, which production numbers to pull first, the failures it adds and how to pilot one with a rollback.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Trunk-Based Development: Merge Small, Merge Daily
posts.summary: Trunk-based development keeps branches short and merges small changes daily. What DORA found, how flags hide unfinished work, and the review and test habits it needs.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: How to Get Unstuck From Analysis Paralysis
posts.summary: Research that started as care can turn into a way to avoid choosing. Sort one-way from two-way doors, ask what would change your mind, and run a timeboxed spike.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Reducing Hallucinations in LLMs, One Layer at a Time
posts.summary: Hallucinations rarely look wrong. How to cut them in a real AI feature: tighter tasks, better retrieval, quote-backed citations, room to say 'I don't know' and evals.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Mentorship vs Sponsorship: Who Talks With You, Who Speaks Up for You
posts.summary: A mentor gives you advice. A sponsor puts your name forward in rooms you're not in. What the research says, small ways to sponsor, and how to make your work easy to back.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Event Sourcing for Beginners: Keep the Whole Story
posts.summary: Event Sourcing stores every change as an event and rebuilds state from that history. How it works, what it buys you, what it costs, and where plain CRUD is fine.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Is TDD Worth the Time? What the Evidence Says
posts.summary: TDD costs time up front and pays it back on some code, not all. What the studies found, where test-first earns its keep, where it gets in the way, and how to decide.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Reading Code Is Harder Than Writing It
posts.summary: Developers spend most of their time understanding code, and that counts as real work. How to trace one path, pin behavior with a test and hold off on the rewrite.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Prompting, RAG or Fine-Tuning? Name the Failure First
posts.summary: Prompting fixes unclear instructions, RAG fixes missing knowledge and fine-tuning fixes behavior a model can't hold. How to tell which failure you're actually looking at.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Onboarding That Actually Helps New Teammates
posts.summary: Good onboarding gives new teammates a map, a buddy, small real tasks and a safe place to ask. What to prepare, what research says, and how to tell if it's working.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Saga Pattern, or How to Undo Half a Checkout
posts.summary: A saga splits one business transaction into local steps, each with a way back. How to order steps around the pivot, choose orchestration or choreography and debug it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Retros That Actually Change How the Team Works
posts.summary: Most retros end with a wall of notes and no next move. How to pick one small experiment, give it an owner, keep it safe to speak up, and check next week that it worked.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What Junior Developers Actually Need From a Mentor
posts.summary: New grads can code. They get stuck on context and on asking for help. How to brief a task, show your reasoning, allow safe mistakes and read their questions as signals.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Ethics in AI Products Starts in the Feature Brief
posts.summary: AI ethics is mostly product work: consent, data limits, fairness checks, real human review, honest explanations and harm metrics, plus the laws in force as of Nov 2026.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Async Communication for Remote Teams
posts.summary: A remote team runs on messages someone can act on half a day later. How to write the whole thought, record decisions, set reply tiers and leave a handoff that works.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: What Belongs in Your API Gateway (and What Doesn't)
posts.summary: What an API gateway should own (routing, token checks, rate limits, tracing), when a BFF earns its keep, and how to keep the gateway from becoming your next monolith.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: RAG Basics: Search First, Answer Second
posts.summary: How retrieval-augmented generation works, from chunks and embeddings to cited answers, and how to tell which layer broke when a RAG answer comes back wrong.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Case for a Boring Tech Stack
posts.summary: Boring tech is tech whose failure modes you already know. Why that helps on-call, hiring and maintenance, how to spend innovation tokens, and when boring turns into debt.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Hexagonal Architecture on One Real Feature, Start to Finish
posts.summary: One refund button, built the hexagonal way: write the rule as a sentence, name ports after the feature, test the core with fakes, and know when to skip it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Writing Acceptance Criteria People Can Actually Test
posts.summary: Acceptance criteria are the written trace of a conversation. Where they come from, how to make them observable, which edge cases matter, and when Given/When/Then helps.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Kanban or Scrum? Start With How Work Reaches Your Team
posts.summary: Kanban and Scrum answer different questions. Pick by looking at how work arrives, how much is in progress and what kind of promise your stakeholders need.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Perfect Code Is the Wrong Target
posts.summary: One more polish pass on working code feels like care, yet it mostly delays feedback. Why better beats perfect, and how to aim for code your team can review and change.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Why Long AI Chats Lose the Thread
posts.summary: Bigger context windows still degrade as they fill up. What the research says about long inputs, and how to keep a working set, write state notes and restart chats.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: When Your Best Engineer Is Hard to Work With
posts.summary: Fast, skilled and hard to work with. What research says about the cost of one harmful teammate, why teams keep paying it, and how to set boundaries with room to repair.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Hiring for Potential or Experience? Look at the Evidence First
posts.summary: Years of experience predict job performance only weakly. How to weigh potential against experience using real evidence, the team's next year and the coaching you have.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: How Much Testing Does an AI Answer Need?
posts.summary: An AI answer is a claim until something outside the model backs it up. How to size the check to the cost of being wrong, with a bug walkthrough, a table and a PR note.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Why Good Preparation Looks Like Nothing Happened
posts.summary: Good prep shows up as a release nobody remembers. Why teams reward firefighting over prevention, how a premortem helps, and how to leave a trace of the work behind it.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Daily Standup That Changes Decisions
posts.summary: A standup where everyone updates but nothing gets decided has done half its job. How to end yours with a clear call: what finishes first, what waits, who helps whom.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: The Best AI Ideas Start in Your Most Boring Chores
posts.summary: Useful AI ideas come from the chores you repeat every week. How to split work into reading and deciding, test the jagged frontier and pilot with a human gate.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong

posts.title: Event-Driven Architecture, Explained Without the Hype
posts.summary: When to call a service and when to publish an event, what brokers really guarantee, how to survive duplicate messages, and when events only add complexity.
posts.author: Nguyen Le Phong
